identity.title: Starbursts with suppressed velocity dispersion revealed in a forming cluster at z = 2.51

paper_type_evidence.quote: Here we report spatially resolved Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) observations of the CO $J= 3-2$ emission line, with a resolution of about 2.5 kiloparsecs, toward a forming galaxy cluster core with starburst galaxies at $z=2.51$.

findings_qualitative.value: The two cluster starburst galaxies (SB1 and SB2) host regular, rotation-dominated, dynamically cold gas-rich disks without clear evidence of major mergers.

evidence.quote: In contrast to starburst galaxies in the field often associated with galaxy mergers or highly turbulent gaseous disks, our observations show that the two starbursts in the cluster exhibit dynamically cold (rotation-dominated) gas-rich disks.

evidence.loc: Triggering mechanism of high-$z$ cluster starburst
evidence.quote: Their intrinsic velocity dispersions are extremely low, with $\sigma_{\rm 0} \sim 20-30$ km s$^{-1}$, while the two MSs have $\sigma_{\rm 0} \sim 90-110$ km s$^{-1}$ (see Table [\[summary\]](#summary)).

findings_qualitative.value: The combination of high gas fractions (~0.7) and suppressed velocity dispersions makes the gas disks of the two cluster starbursts gravitationally unstable (Toomre Q << Q_crit), triggering intense star formation.

evidence.quote: The high gas fraction and suppressed velocity dispersion yield gravitationally unstable gas disks, which enables highly efficient star formation.

evidence.loc: Triggering mechanism of high-$z$ cluster starburst
evidence.quote: However, in our case, the two SBs have much lower Toomre $Q$ values than $Q_{\rm crit}$ and they have high gas fractions ($\sim$0.7; see Table [\[tab3\]](#tab3)).

findings_qualitative.value: The two cluster starbursts do not show compact gas disks according to the submillimeter compactness criterion, and show negligible AGN contribution (<0.2%) to their IR SEDs.

evidence.loc: Structural properties of the molecular gas
evidence.quote: By further using the submillimeter compactness criterion (cite: Puglisi2021), which is used to select compact galaxies, defined as a ratio of the stellar size (cite: vanderWel2014) larger than the molecular gas size by a factor of 2.2, we conclude that the two SBs do not show compact gas disks.
We did not find any sign of a significant contribution of an AGN ($f_{\rm AGN}<0.2 \%$) in the infrared SEDs of our two SBs and two MSs, in agreement with previous literature constraints ().

claims.hypothesis: Starburst galaxies in the forming cluster CLJ1001 at z = 2.51 are triggered by mergers or violent interactions that produce turbulent, dynamically hot gas disks, similar to field starbursts.
claims.experiment: Perform spatially resolved (~0.3'', ~2.5 kpc) ALMA CO(3-2) observations and 3D kinematic modeling with GalPAK^3D on two starburst (SB1, SB2) and two main-sequence (MS1, MS2) galaxies in CLJ1001.
claims.result: Both SBs exhibit regular rotating disks with V_max/sigma_0 of 16.8 (+7.4/-10.4) and 15.0 (+13.0/-11.3), and intrinsic velocity dispersions sigma_0 of 25 (+11/-15) km/s and 33 (+27/-19) km/s, which are three times lower than field counterparts and cluster MS galaxies (sigma_0 ~ 90-110 km/s).
claims.finding: Refuted; the cluster starbursts host dynamically cold, rotation-dominated disks with suppressed velocity dispersion rather than merger-driven turbulent disks.

evidence.quote: In contrast to starburst galaxies in the field often associated with galaxy mergers or highly turbulent gaseous disks, our observations show that the two starbursts in the cluster exhibit dynamically cold (rotation-dominated) gas-rich disks.

evidence.loc: The two SBs have dynamically cold gas-rich disks with low velocity dispersions
evidence.quote: The gas disks of the two SBs are rotation-dominated with gas rotational to random motion ratios ($V_{\mathrm{max}}/\sigma_{\mathrm{0}}$) of 16.8$^{+7.4}_{-10.4}$ and 15.0$^{+13.0}_{-11.3}$, while the two MSs have a $V_{\mathrm{max}}/\sigma_{\mathrm{0}}$ of 3.6$^{+1.1}_{-0.9}$ and 2.2$^{+2.0}_{-1.2}$

claims.hypothesis: Self-gravitational instability of the gas disks, induced by high gas fractions and suppressed velocity dispersions, triggers the efficient starburst activity in the two cluster starbursts.
claims.experiment: Derive molecular gas masses using three independent methods (CO(1-0), dust mass with delta_GDR, and 3.2 mm RJ continuum) and compute the Toomre Q parameter using kinematic parameters from GalPAK^3D.
claims.result: The two SBs have high gas fractions (f_gas ~ 0.7) and Toomre Q values well below Q_crit (both for thin disk Q_crit = 1 and thick disk Q_crit = 0.67, even if adopting alpha_CO,SB = 0.8), with Q decreasing as main-sequence offset increases.
claims.finding: Supported; the combination of high gas fraction and suppressed velocity dispersion yields gravitationally unstable gas disks that collapse to drive efficient star formation.

evidence.loc: The two SBs have gravitationally unstable gas disks
evidence.quote: The two SBs present $Q$ values much smaller than $Q_{\rm crit}$. We note that using the local starbursts’ conversion factor ($\alpha_{\rm CO, SB}$ = 0.8 $M_{\odot}$(K km s$^{-1}$ pc$^{2}$)$^{-1}$) for the two SBs, the derived Toomre parameter $Q$ values increase by a factor of five but still remain below $Q_{\rm crit}$.

evidence.loc: Triggering mechanism of high-$z$ cluster starburst
evidence.quote: Thus, the most possible mechanism for inducing efficient star formation activity in the two cluster SBs is the self-gravitational instability of gas disks caused by the low $\sigma_{0}$ (and the high gas fractions).

claims.hypothesis: Corotating and coplanar cold gas accretion, rather than post-merger disk rebuilding, is responsible for the high gas fractions and low velocity dispersions in the two cluster starbursts.
claims.experiment: Compare the observed gas fractions, intrinsic velocity dispersions, disk sizes, and HST/F160W + CO(3-2) morphologies against theoretical predictions for cold stream accretion and gas-rich major merger remnants.
claims.result: The SBs show extended gas disks (r_1/2 = 1.79 and 1.29 kpc), high rotational velocities (V_max ~ 400-500 km/s), low sigma_0, high gas fractions (~0.7), and no morphological signs of major mergers in CO(3-2) or HST/F160W.
claims.finding: Supported; the properties conflict with compact, turbulent post-merger disks and favor accretion of corotating and coplanar cold gas streams.

evidence.loc: Drivers of low turbulent gas in the two cluster SBs
evidence.quote: The two SBs favor a scenario in which cold gas is accreted via corotating and coplanar streams (cite: Danovich2012; Danovich2015).

evidence.loc: Drivers of low turbulent gas in the two cluster SBs
evidence.quote: Thus, the high gas fraction, low $\sigma_{0}$, and lack of evidence for galaxy major mergers in the two SBs appear inconsistent with merger remnants.

why_this_data.value: CLJ1001 at z=2.51 is in rapid transformation from a protocluster to a mature cluster; combining compact (C40-4) and extended (C40-7) ALMA configurations provides both reliable total flux measurements and spatially/spectroscopically resolved (~2.5 kpc) CO(3-2) kinematics.

evidence.quote: CLJ1001 is in the phase of rapid transformation from a protocluster to a mature cluster, which makes it an ideal laboratory to study the connection between the triggering mechanism of cluster starbursts and their dense environment.

We adopted two different array configurations to obtain reliable measurements of total flux and resolved kinematics information: a more compact array configuration (C40-4) observing low-resolution large spatial scales, while a more extended array configuration (C40-7) observing high-resolution small spatial scales

why_this_method.value: UV-plane fitting (uvmodelfit) avoids imaging uncertainties for sizes; CO(1-0) + three independent gas mass estimators avoid CO excitation and conversion factor biases; 3D forward modeling with GalPAK^3D accounts for 3D PSF and LSF beam smearing.

evidence.loc: Structural properties of the molecular gas
evidence.quote: To avoid uncertainties from the imaging process, we derived the source sizes with the visibility CO(3$-$2) data in the $UV$ plane by fitting an elliptical Gaussian (task $uvmodelfit$).
To obtain the total molecular gas mass $M_{\rm gas,CO}$, we used the CO(1$-$0) luminosity () instead of CO(3$-$2) to avoid uncertainties caused by the CO excitation ladder.

The model is convolved with a 3D kernel to account for the instrument point spread function (PSF) and the line spread function (LSF) smearing effect. GalPAK$^{3D}$ can thus return intrinsic galaxy properties.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Local starburst CO-to-H2 conversion factor (alpha_CO,SB = 0.8): rejected as primary choice because it yields unphysically low gas-to-dust ratios (delta_GDR ~ 20), though tested to confirm main conclusions and Q < Q_crit still hold.

evidence.quote: However, using $\alpha_{\rm CO, SB}$ = 0.8 $M_{\odot}$(K km s$^{-1}$ pc$^{2}$)$^{-1}$ for the two SBs would result in very low gas-to-dust ratios ($\delta_{\rm GDR}$$\sim$20), making the two SBs extreme cases.

We however show that even if we had chosen a local SB conversion factor ($\alpha_{\rm CO, SB}$ = 0.8 $M_{\odot}$(K km s$^{-1}$ pc$^{2}$)$^{-1}$) for the two SBs, the main conclusions of the paper would remain unchanged.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Native ~12 km s^-1 channel width data cubes for final kinematic parameters: tested and found consistent with 30 km s^-1 cubes, but rejected in favor of 30 km s^-1 cubes which have better sensitivity to detect fainter galaxy edges.

evidence.quote: We applied the same analysis to the data cubes under the original channel width of $\sim$12 km s$^{-1}$. The results were consistent with each other within errors. Therefore, considering that a better sensitivity can help detect fainter galaxy edges and better sample the flat part of the rotation curves, we have adopted the values from the data cubes with a channel width of 30 km s$^{-1}$ in this work.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Direct parameter uncertainties output by GalPAK^3D: rejected because injection-recovery simulations showed they were underestimated by a factor of 5; simulation-derived uncertainties were adopted instead.

evidence.quote: In general, there is no global offset of the derived values from the GalPAK$^{3D}$, but the uncertainty is greatly underestimated by a factor of 5. Thus, we use the uncertainties of $\sigma_{\rm 0}$ and $V_{\rm max}$ given by this simulation in the main body of this paper

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Rapidly reformed rotating disks after final coalescence of gas-rich major mergers: considered as an alternative explanation for high gas fractions, but rejected because post-merger disks are predicted to be compact and highly turbulent.

evidence.loc: Drivers of low turbulent gas in the two cluster SBs
evidence.quote: However, simulations of gas-rich major mergers reveal enhanced gas turbulence and reduced sizes of disk components that survive or that one rebuilt after a merger (cite: Bournaud2011), which conflicts with the observed low $\sigma_{\mathrm{0}}$ and relatively extended disk sizes of the two SBs.

how_they_decided_enough.value: Checked MCMC convergence over 20,000 iterations, verified consistency between 30 km/s and native ~12 km/s channel cubes, and ran 100 injection-recovery simulations per galaxy to calibrate parameter uncertainties.

evidence.quote: We also plotted the full MCMC chain from GalPAK$^{3D}$ for the two SBs and two MSs with 20,000 iterations to confirm the convergence of rotational velocity and intrinsic velocity dispersion (Fig. [3](#ed1)).
We applied the same analysis to the data cubes under the original channel width of $\sim$12 km s$^{-1}$. The results were consistent with each other within errors.
Then, we ran the GalPAK$^{3D}$ to derive $\sigma_{\rm 0}$ and $V_{\rm max}$. These two steps were repeated 100 times for each galaxy.

limitations_admitted.value: MS2 shows different CO(3-2) sizes between image-plane and UV-plane analyses due to its lower detection significance (10 sigma), and 3.2 mm dust continuum sizes could not be measured for SB2, MS1, and MS2 due to low S/N.

evidence.loc: Structural properties of the molecular gas
evidence.quote: We note that MS2 shows different sizes in the imaging and $UV$ analyses, which could be caused by its lowest significance ($10\sigma$) of (3$-$2) detections among the four sources.

evidence.loc: Structural properties of the molecular gas
evidence.quote: For the dust size, we only successfully measured the SB1 in the image plane, which has the highest signal-to-noise ratio ($S/N\sim8$) of 3.2 mm dust continuum emission among the four sources.

limitations_admitted.value: Higher-J CO transitions (e.g., CO(5-4) and CO(6-5)) are lacking and needed to determine whether the warm/dense gas in the two SBs is highly excited or MS-like.

evidence.quote: The higher-$J$ CO transition observations (e.g., CO(5$-$4) and CO(6$-$5) probing warm and dense molecular gas) are necessary to establish whether the gas in the two SBs is highly excited as expected in starburst galaxies, or less excited as in MS galaxies.

limitations_admitted.value: Some points in the 1D rotation velocity and velocity dispersion profiles deviate from the dynamical models because of flux contamination by neighboring sources.

evidence.quote: Some points deviate from the models because of the flux contamination by neighboring sources.

limitations_admitted.value: Formal uncertainties from GalPAK^3D are underestimated by a factor of 5, and the possibility that the two SBs are caught in the short final coalescence stage of gas-rich mergers cannot be completely ruled out.

evidence.quote: In general, there is no global offset of the derived values from the GalPAK$^{3D}$, but the uncertainty is greatly underestimated by a factor of 5.

evidence.loc: Drivers of low turbulent gas in the two cluster SBs
evidence.quote: While the possibility cannot be fully ruled out that the two SBs are in the final coalescence stage of gas-rich mergers, the chance that both SBs are caught in this short stage is small.

referee_caveats_inferred: The low inclination of SB2 (19.30 deg) introduces large degeneracy in V_max (497 +123/-252 km/s), which propagates into V_max/sigma_0 and the epicyclic frequency kappa in Toomre Q.

The best-fit intrinsic velocity dispersion of SB1 (25 km/s) is below the adopted 30 km/s channel width and only ~2 times the native ~12 km/s channel width, making it sensitive to line spread function assumptions.
Sample size is small (two starbursts and two main-sequence galaxies in a single cluster), limiting statistical generalization to all high-z protoclusters.

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~10-30 GB (single pointing ALMA Band 3 observations in two configurations, ~7 hours total execution time)
reproducibility.score_reason: Calibration, array combination weights, pixel sizes, channel widths, weighting schemes, and kinematic modeling tools/assumptions are clearly specified, and all key output quantities are tabulated. Minor deductions for missing tclean stopping criteria, exact continuum line-free channel ranges, and GalPAK^3D prior bounds.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Public ALMA dataset (2016.1.01155.S), well-defined recipe from calibrated visibilities to 3D kinematic modeling with public software (CASA, CIGALE, GalPAK^3D), and comprehensive numeric tables for fluxes, sizes, masses, V_max, and sigma_0.
